scope: A deterministic Linux capability confirmation for direct Camoufox control and a Model Context Protocol path. It is not product support, an arbitrary-site benchmark, an anti-detection claim, or permission to remove Dolly's Module startup refusal.
priorDevelopmentObservations: The immutable v0 preregistration mixed deterministic browser control with an optional model-driven condition and is not reused as the confirmation claim.

Development runs retained under artifacts/experiments/probes/camoufox-mcp-v0 showed that @playwright/mcp 0.0.79 was incompatible with Camoufox's Playwright 1.60 server, 0.0.74 rejected a later-only CLI option, a remote browser with no context required --isolated, and the 1.60 alpha client protocol was not compatible with the stable 1.60 server.
The candidate selected for this confirmation pins @playwright/mcp 0.0.74 while overriding both of its Playwright dependencies to stable 1.60.0, exactly matching the Python Playwright server version.
question: With exact protocol versions frozen, can both the direct Camoufox Python API and a real MCP SDK client through Microsoft Playwright MCP control the same Camoufox browser on Linux for screenshots, text input, clicking, explicit scrolling, state inspection, a deliberate missing-target failure, and same-session recovery in three fresh repetitions?

hypotheses.null: At least one backend has fewer than three complete independently verified cases, or the MCP path does not exercise every required tool and recover in the same page session.
hypotheses.alternative: Both backends have three of three complete independently verified cases and the MCP path exercises every required tool, produces both screenshots, observes the deliberate error, and recovers without replacing the page session.

decisionBoundary.ifAlternative: Keep the exact-version MCP-to-Camoufox path as a candidate read/write browser tool adapter and keep direct Camoufox as a deterministic baseline. Next work must still define host-owned tool policy, filesystem/network scope, credentials, budgets, and Module lifecycle before product integration.
decisionBoundary.ifNullAndDirectPasses: Do not call direct Camoufox evidence MCP evidence. Reject the selected MCP compatibility set and isolate the failed protocol or tool operation before another versioned confirmation.
decisionBoundary.ifBothFail: Do not retain either path as a Linux candidate from this experiment.
cannotDecide: production support or removal of RUNTIME_MODULE_MIGRATION_REQUIRED
arbitrary-site success, model planning, screenshot understanding by a model, login/session safety, anti-detection quality, or cross-platform behavior
whether browser tools with external effects are crash-safe or authorized for a long-lived Module

baseline.reason: It separates browser/Camoufox feasibility from MCP transport, schema, and remote Playwright behavior.

backends.path: Python runner -> Camoufox Python API -> Camoufox browser
MCP SDK over stdio -> Microsoft Playwright MCP -> Playwright WebSocket -> Camoufox browser

data.description: One repository-local deterministic HTML document with solid-color screenshot anchors, an input, three state-changing buttons, an off-screen action, and a page-instance timestamp.

randomization.interpretation: The direct runner seeds Python and NumPy. The MCP runner records the seed as a repetition identity but makes no random choice. Browser fingerprint internals are not assumed to obey these seeds. Order is fixed because latency is diagnostic only.

steps: start a fresh local fixture server and a fresh Camoufox browser path
navigate to the loopback fixture and establish successful page readiness
type the exact input and click Apply once
inspect and retain the resulting page state
explicitly scroll to the document bottom, click Bottom once, and inspect state
attempt the deliberately missing target exactly once and require an error
click Recover once without replacing the page and verify all prior state plus the same pageTimeOrigin
close only exact process identities created and recorded by this case

screenshotOracle.hashRule: Every PNG byte length and SHA-256 is recorded and checked for integrity. Cross-case PNG hashes need not be equal; exact dimensions and anchor pixels are the visual correctness oracle.

environment.isolation: HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, TMPDIR, npm_config_cache, PIP_CACHE_DIR, and Python bytecode cache are explicitly placed under /home/ubuntu/codex-dolly. Browser cases receive no HTTP or HTTPS proxy and set both NO_PROXY variants to exactly 127.0.0.1,localhost.
environment.network: Cases use only an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 HTTP fixture and local stdio/WebSocket connections. This confirmation makes no LLM, provider, OSS, or external website request.

primary: complete independently verified cases out of three per backend
required MCP tool inventory and successful exercise per case
top and bottom PNG dimension plus exact anchor pixels per case
exact input and state counters after each action
deliberate error observed and same pageTimeOrigin retained through recovery
remaining recorded process identities at case finalization
metrics.minimumEffectiveDifference: One complete case out of three, or 33.33 percentage points. Latency cannot change the v1 decision.

stopRules: Run exactly three fresh repetitions per backend unless that backend has two consecutive browser or protocol initialization failures.
After two consecutive initialization failures, retain both raw files, stop only that backend, and label it infrastructure-inconclusive.
Do not retry a failed action inside a case. The Recover click after the deliberate error is a planned action, not a retry.

If any fixture, runner, dependency, or verifier defect is found after confirmation execution starts, preserve the run, version the correction, freeze new implementation hashes, and use a new run directory.
Never replace failed MCP operations with direct calls or simulated MCP results.

evidence.independentVerification: The verifier imports no runner code. It checks frozen source bytes, exact inventory, raw JSONL sequences and semantic records, PNG bytes/dimensions/pixels, process finalization, and orchestration exits. Runner summary booleans are necessary but never sufficient.
